notes: The manuscript continues a discussion of the modular curve over the marked moduli space, with four named sections and an S4 action exchanging them. It says the construction will not be carried out here and would produce the unmarked modular multiplicities. These are manuscript claims; this page reading does not establish them mathematically.

The manuscript replaces diagram (76) by numerical diagram (78), with a codimension-zero vertex labeled 4 and a codimension-one two-vertex graph labeled 2,2, linked by an arrow labeled 1. It states that the unmarked space has a single point at infinity corresponding to the three points at infinity of the marked space, permuted transitively by S4. No independent proof of the quotient or its cusp count was performed.

Under the heading on fractional Euler–Poincaré characteristics, the manuscript writes the first two characteristic values −1 and 2, then a quotient-style characteristic and a decomposition using the exceptional sets {−bar j,−j} and {1/2,2,−1}. It ends with −1+1/3+1/2=−1/(24|6), with the denominator overwritten and unresolved. The separate NB writes division of chi_!(U an) by [S4], with result −1/24. The geometric equalities and any weighting convention were not independently proved.

A targeted exact-rational calculation in Python fractions.Fraction gives −1+1/3+1/2=−1/6, which differs from −1/24 by −1/8. Thus a final denominator 24 would make the displayed numerical equality false as written. The transcription preserves the written terms and the denominator doubt. This calculation neither supplies an omitted factor nor settles the overworked digits; no claim is made that all summands should be divided by 24.

Source forms retained include Je vais pas without ne, the future form donnera, literal du = coup, the abbreviations pt/pts and EP, and the final point-set contribution’s curved ) with no comma before S4. The malformed delimiter is not silently balanced.
